objective.wording: Orient a spinal cord specimen and identify its external landmarks.
Compare the lower extent of the cord in a child and an adult on labelled diagrams and explain one implication of the difference.
Sketch and label mid-cervical and mid-thoracic sections and identify features that distinguish them.
Sort the main pathways represented at mid-thoracic level by direction of transmission.
Use a simulated motor examination to explain the spinal grey-matter localization considered in poliomyelitis.
Use a simulated motor examination to identify upper and lower motor neuron findings and explain the spinal structures considered in motor neuron disease.
Use a labelled spinal cord section to connect the distribution of findings in a simulated syringomyelia case to affected structures.
Identify which structures in the sensory pathway could account for the findings in a simulated hereditary sensory neuropathy case.
Use a simulated examination to explain which cord pathways could account for the combination of findings.
Use a simulated neurological examination to propose a spinal level and explain the findings that support it.
Use the examination in a simulated paraplegia case to compare possible anatomical localizations.
Describe the findings expected in a simulated complete transection and explain how the level changes the presentation.
Use preserved and impaired functions in a simulated case to explain why an incomplete transection pattern is considered.
Trace the spinal portions of selected ascending pathways and identify which sensory modalities each pathway carries.
Trace selected descending pathways through the spinal cord and identify where they connect with motor circuits.
